Subject: Post-call: Finwise load test coordination & SLO confirmation

Hi Dana / Tom —

Thanks again for the call earlier — good to align on the SLO targets and the test plan. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get the customer-led load test scheduled:

Recap of SLOs you asked us to qualify:
- Target latency (95th): <= 300 ms for standard text generation when using streaming responses;
- Throughput target: sustained 200 requests/sec for peak path;
- Concurrency: up to 150 concurrent clients (expected ramp to peak over 20m);
- Streaming requirements: server-sent-events (SSE) style streaming for partial tokens; ensure client handles chunked frames.

Customer-led load test plan (proposed):
1) Provide you a sample k6 script tuned to your workload and an alternative Locust script if you prefer.
2) We provide a short-lived test account + API key and a list of staging endpoints to exercise.
3) You run the load test from your environment (we'll provide IPs to allowlist).
4) Redwood monitoring will collect metrics (latency percentiles, token throughput, error rate) and we will join Zoom/Slack during the window to observe and iterate.

Proposed test window: Wednesday, 3 Mar 2027, 10:00–12:00 PT (10:00–12:00). Please confirm if that works for your team and which of your IP blocks will be used so we can add to the allowlist.

Attachments: sample k6 script (finwise_k6_sample.js), proposed allowlist format (finwise_ip_allowlist.txt), and a template for test account creds (finwise_test_account_credentials.txt).

Next steps if you confirm the window:
- We will provision the test account and share creds 24h prior.
- Aditya will be on the test for any runtime questions and to adjust quotas.
- Logan will share monitoring dashboards and the zoom link.

Thanks — I’ll wait for confirmation and the IP list.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Dana — looping in a couple of quick technical details so your infra team can configure the test environment: 

- API host / endpoints: https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate (streaming via /v1/generate?stream=true) — use the Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY> header.
- Streaming behavior: SSE-style framed tokens; client should keep connection open and handle reconnections. For k6 we include an example that opens long-lived connections with a 10s keep-alive.
- Rate limiting / quotas: test account will be on an elevated quota for the 2h window but still subject to per-client concurrency limits; we’ll disable global throttles for the test window to avoid preemption.
- Expected behavior during ramp: during initial ramp we may see 95p latency in the 300–350ms range while caches warm; once warmed we expect to get below 300ms for the main path.

Attachments: finwise_k6_sample.js (k6 script w/ streaming scenario), finwise_test_account_credentials.txt (test API key + endpoints), finwise_ip_allowlist.txt (format for your firewall team).

If you can send the IP blocks, we’ll add them to the allowlist today and provision the test key ~24h prior to the window. I’ll be on call during the window for realtime tuning (token bucket, batching knobs).

— Aditya
Aditya Rao
Senior Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com
